title: Extraction of Microbial Cells from Methane-Seep Carbonate Rocks for Single-Cell Analyses
author: Magdalena J Mayr
materials: Make sure all solutions are filtered 0.2 μm the same day, e.g. using a syringe filter.

steps.title: Fix rock sample
steps.instruction: Place the small piece or crushed carbonate rock in 2 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) prepared in 3× PBS (marine samples) and incubate overnight at 4 °C. Use appropriate PPE and dispose of PFA waste safely.

steps.title: Thaw and chill sample
steps.instruction: Remove the frozen sample from the freezer and immediately place it on ice.

steps.title: Wash rocks to remove contamination
steps.instruction: Choose one of the following washing strategies and perform the washes three times before crushing the rock.

substeps.instruction: Option 1 – Sonication: Transfer carbonate into freshly filtered 1× PBS, sonicate with a wand for 2 × 15 s, discard the supernatant into a fresh tube, repeat wash three times, then crush the rock with a clean mortar and pestle.
Option 2 – Vortex/shake: If the rock is too crumbly for sonication, place it in freshly filtered 1× PBS in a fresh tube, shake or vortex three times, then proceed to crushing.
Option 3 – Surface removal: Use a diamond saw or rotary tool with a diamond wheel to remove the rock surface when many cells are needed, then wash the interior using Option 1 or Option 2.

steps.title: Clean mortar and pestle
steps.instruction: Remove visible dirt, rinse thoroughly with de‑ionised (DI) water, wipe with RNase‑away, then wipe with 70 % ethanol using clean Kimwipes.

steps.title: Crush rock to paste
steps.instruction: Using the cleaned mortar and pestle, crush the rock piece to a fine paste.

steps.title: Weigh crushed carbonate
steps.instruction: Add approximately 0.1 g of the crushed carbonate to a pre‑weighed 2 mL snap‑cap tube. Record the weight after addition to estimate the amount of rock used. Do not overload the subsequent Percoll centrifugation; scale tube size if more rock is needed.

steps.title: Add combination buffer
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of freshly filtered “combination buffer” (see buffer recipe step) to the tube containing rock. Keep the tube on ice.

substeps.instruction: Sonicate the tube with a probe for 3 × 10 s, pausing 10 s between pulses to avoid heating; clean the sonicator between samples (Qsonica Q55, lowest setting 10).
Place the tube on a vortex adapter (e.g., MOBIO/Qiagen) and shake gently for 30 min while kept on ice.

steps.title: Pre‑chill all reagents
steps.instruction: Place ethanol, Percoll and any other reagents on ice; do not skip this step.

steps.title: Add cold ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 450 µL of 4 °C ethanol to the tube and keep on ice for 5 min before proceeding.

steps.title: Layer Percoll under mixture
steps.instruction: Slowly pipette 950 µL of 4 °C Percoll to the bottom of the tube so that it forms a distinct layer beneath the combination‑buffer/ethanol/rock/cell suspension.

steps.title: Density‑gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 4 °C, 18 000 g for 20 min using a refrigerated centrifuge (or a centrifuge placed in a fridge). After spin, place the tube on water ice.

steps.title: Collect cell‑rich interface
steps.instruction: After centrifugation you should see (from bottom to top): rock pellet, Percoll phase, a fluffy “cell interface”, and supernatant. Pipette the supernatant and the fluffy interface into a fresh tube, avoiding any Percoll. Keep the tube with the rock pellet for later weighing.

steps.title: Optional second Percoll gradient
steps.instruction: If a second gradient is required, repeat the following steps.

substeps.instruction: Fill the rock‑pellet tube to 1 mL with cold 4 °C ethanol and keep on ice.
Vortex briefly, then add 950 µL of 4 °C Percoll to the bottom of the tube.
Place the tube on ice and pipette off supernatant and fluffy interface into a fresh tube, avoiding Percoll.

steps.title: Wash extracted cells
steps.instruction: Wash the collected cell fraction at least twice with 1× PBS (or 3× PBS) and then store the cells in a 30:70 (v/v) mixture of 1× PBS:Ethanol. Keep the suspension overnight at 4 °C to allow ethanol penetration, then transfer to –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Optional storage in 50:50 PBS/Ethanol
steps.instruction: If desired, keep extracted cells in a 50:50 (v/v) mixture of 1× PBS:Ethanol (note that this may work variably for rock‑derived cells).

steps.title: Pellet cells with Nanopure water
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL Nanopure water to the cell suspension and centrifuge at 20 000 g for 3 min.

steps.title: Remove supernatant, retain cells
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant, leaving approximately 100 µL of liquid to avoid loss of the cell pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend and repeat wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 900 µL of 1× PBS, vortex gently, then centrifuge again at 20 000 g for 3 min. Repeat the removal‑resuspend steps once more.

steps.title: Final cell resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final cell pellet in 25–400 µL of 1× PBS. If needed, pipette up and down with a 1 mL pipette to achieve a homogeneous suspension.

steps.title: Prepare filtration apparatus
steps.instruction: Clean a glass funnel or a 12‑well Millipore vacuum filtration unit. Place a supporting filter (e.g., 5 µm pore size) followed by a 0.2 µm polycarbonate filter (white for FISH, black for DAPI) of 25 mm diameter on top.

steps.title: Add PBS to filtration wells
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of 0.2 µm pre‑filtered 1× PBS to each well of the filtration unit.

steps.title: Measure cell‑extract volume
steps.instruction: If you are not using the entire extract, measure the total volume remaining for later cell‑number calculations.

steps.title: Load cells onto filter
steps.instruction: Add 100–1 000 µL of the cell extract to each well (record the exact volume) and apply ~200 mbar pressure to drive the suspension through the filter.

steps.title: Wash filter
steps.instruction: Wash each filter with approximately 2 × 5 mL of 1× PBS followed by 1 × 5 mL of Nanopure water (more if needed). Avoid transferring any residual Percoll; if a layer forms on the filter, wash the cells further before mounting.

steps.title: Dry and label filters
steps.instruction: Label each filter with a pencil, place them in a small petri dish and dry at 40 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Check extraction with DAPI
steps.instruction: For each filter (e.g., 1/8th of a filter) add 10–15 µL of DAPI‑Citifluor mix and examine under a fluorescence microscope to confirm cell recovery before proceeding to BONCAT or FISH.

steps.title: Proceed to microscopy or storage
steps.instruction: Either continue with microscopy/FISH/BONCAT or store the filters at 4 °C for short‑term or –20 °C for long‑term preservation.

steps.title: Final cell‑pellet clean‑up
steps.instruction: Spin down the cell suspension again at 20 000 g for 3 min, orient tubes consistently, remove liquid leaving 100–200 µL, add 1 mL Nanopure water and repeat the wash three times. Keep the final pellet in 20–300 µL depending on cell numbers; if the pellet does not resuspend, sonicate briefly in a bath.

steps.title: Spot cells on poly‑L‑lysine slide
steps.instruction: Place 5–8 µL of the cell suspension onto a poly‑L‑lysine‑coated 10‑well slide, dry at 40 °C for 10–15 min, then store the slide at 4 °C until further processing (BONCAT/FISH).

steps.title: DAPI staining on slide
steps.instruction: Add ~3.5 µL of DAPI‑Citifluor mix to each well of the slide, cover with a large coverslip, and check cell density and extraction success before downstream assays. Use only one sample and one FISH probe per slide to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Recover rock pellet for weight
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the rock pellet with any remaining Percoll layer for 3 min at 20 000 g, discard Percoll, wash the pellet once with 1 mL Nanopure water, centrifuge again, discard water, then evaporate residual water at 40 °C (or 27–55 °C) overnight until dry. Record the final dry weight (subtract the pre‑weighed tube weight).

steps.title: Prepare combination buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 % (v/v) Tween 20, 3 mM sodium pyrophosphate, and 0.35 % (w/v) PVP 40000 (or PVPP) in 1× PBS. Filter the solution through a 0.2 µm filter, aliquot under sterile conditions, wrap lids with parafilm and store sterile‑filtered at 4 °C in the dark for weeks to months.

steps.title: Prepare Percoll aliquots
steps.instruction: Aliquot Percoll under sterile laminar‑flow conditions, optionally filter through a 0.2 µm filter, and store at 4 °C. Note that lower supernatant density improves gradient formation; acidic samples may gel.

steps.title: Run extraction controls
steps.instruction: Include a positive control (rock known to contain many cells) and a negative control (no sample or cell‑free calcite) to validate the extraction procedure.

steps.title: Prepare DAPI working solution
steps.instruction: Mix 50 µL of DAPI stock (1 mg mL⁻¹, stored at –20 °C) with 10 mL Citifluor AF1 (EMS cat#17970) and 1 mL 1× PBS (pH 7–7.5, filter‑sterilised) to obtain a final DAPI concentration of 4.5 µg mL⁻¹ (4.5 ng µL⁻¹). The DAPI stock is made by dissolving 10 mg DAPI in 1 mL H₂O, filtering through a 0.2 µm filter.
